outcomes: A gRPC server starts and drains with the rest of the application rather than on its own schedule
A server that configures nothing is still bounded in connection lifetime, keepalive tolerance, and concurrent streams
A web or mobile caller reaches the same operations over Connect that an internal caller reaches over gRPC
Wiring a gateway incompletely is reported at startup instead of surfacing as production 404s
A first-party Connect caller reaches a declared operation with the same values a REST caller reaches it with, over JSON or protobuf
nonGoals: Generating Connect or gRPC stubs, which remain the job of protoc and buf against the published .proto document
Carrying client or bidirectional streams over the api bridge, because Connect carries at most one request message per call
Terminating TLS or mutual TLS, which belongs to the deployment's ingress
Promising strict compatibility between every pre-1.0 minor release

requirements.text: Connection-lifetime, keepalive, and concurrent-stream limits are applied before any caller-supplied server option, so an unconfigured server is bounded by conservative defaults while an explicit option still wins.

Stop runs a graceful drain under a deadline that defaults when unset, and force-closes the server when the deadline elapses so a long-lived stream cannot hang shutdown; stopping a server that never started is a no-op.
Server reflection is disabled unless the workload enables it explicitly, so a deployment does not publish its service catalogue by default.

Unary and stream interceptors run in registration order; the recovery interceptor converts a handler panic into an internal error without leaking the panic value; the dependency-injection interceptor creates one scope per RPC and passes the call through unchanged when no container is available.
Connect handlers become reachable only when the gateway is registered on the HTTP server; a gateway that holds handlers but was never registered warns at start rather than serving nothing silently.

Every bound api endpoint is exposed at a Connect-style RPC URL taken from the published protobuf descriptor when one exists, so the mounted URL and the descriptor's method identity cannot diverge; the bridge refuses to start when they do. Document-only endpoints are skipped, and the JSON envelope keeps path parameters, query parameters, and body in separate sections so identically named fields cannot collide. A mounted bridge publishes the payload encodings it actually serves.

The bridge serves Connect protocol version 1 for a provider that publishes a protobuf descriptor: JSON and protobuf unary bodies, the caller's Connect-Timeout-Ms, gzip bounded in the decompressed direction, the Connect error document carrying the gRPC code beside the stable first-party code in google.rpc.ErrorInfo, and a declared server stream as 5-byte-prefixed envelopes ended by exactly one EndStreamResponse. A codec it does not serve is refused, never guessed at.

A bridged call re-enters the endpoint's own validation pipeline, so it accepts and rejects exactly what the equivalent REST call would, and a numeric path parameter keeps its original decimal text rather than passing through float64.
